stories.title: Law Firm Nutter Expands to 11K SF at Durst’s 5 Grand Central East
stories.excerpt: Law firm Nutter is taking more office space at one of the Durst Organization’s buildings near Grand Central Terminal, Commercial Observer has learned. Nutter, which is based in Boston and provides personal and business legal services, has signed a deal to renew its existing 5,719 square feet on the 27th floor of Durst’s 5 Grand Central East — also known as 655 Third Avenue — and add another 5,719 square feet on the entire 25th floor, according to the landlord. The deal brings the law firm’s total footprint at the 30-story office tower to 11,438 square feet. “The Manhattan office leasing market is surging, especially for Class A spaces in transit-accessible locations such as Grand Central East,” Jody Durst, president of Durst, said in a statement. “Nutter’s decision to expand at 5 Grand Central East reflects the desirability of the area and Durst’s long-term investment in our buildings.” The length of the lease was not provided, but the asking rent was $80 per square foot, according to Durst. CBRE’s Michael Joyce and Trevor Larkin brokered the deal for Nutter, while Durst was repped in-house by Tom Bow, Ashlea Aaron, Bailey Caliban and Sayo Kamara. A spokesperson for CBRE did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Nutter, which was founded in 1879, has been a tenant in Durst’s office building between East 41st and East 42nd streets since 2022. Michael Scott, co-managing partner of Nutter, said in a statement that 5 Grand Central East is “the right location for our clients and our team as we grow.” In December, Durst rebranded two of its office buildings near Grand Central, turning 655 Third Avenue to 5 Grand Central East and renaming 733 Third Avenue as 11 Grand Central East. The rebranding reflected its “continued investment in the Grand Central submarket,” the firm said. bullets: Nutter law firm expands to 11.4K SF at Durst's 5 Grand Central East, Manhattan.
Asking rent $80/SF reflects strong Class A office demand in transit-accessible Midtown.
Tenant renewal + expansion signals confidence in Grand Central submarket despite broader office headwinds.
stories.summary: Boston-based Nutter has renewed and expanded its footprint at 5 Grand Central East (655 Third Avenue) by doubling from 5.7K to 11.4K SF on floors 25–27, at $80/SF asking. Durst Organization highlighted the deal as evidence of surging Manhattan office leasing, especially for Class A transit-proximate space. The expansion signals tenant stickiness and willingness to grow in trophy locations despite sector-wide office challenges.
stories.impact: Strong Class A office fundamentals in Midtown Manhattan—particularly around Grand Central—can drive ancillary multifamily demand (executive relocations, young professional talent retention). However, this is office-focused; minimal direct bearing on multifamily supply or rent unless the market signals broad corporate stability and HQ growth in Manhattan proper.

stories.title: Koeppel Rosen Arranges Three Office Leases in Midtown, Midtown South
stories.excerpt: Koeppel Rosen LLC, leasing and management agent for the Rosen family portfolio, has arranged nearly 18,000 square feet of new office space leases, comprised of separate transactions at three different properties in the company’s portfolio.  Max Koeppel represented Koeppel Rosen in-house on all three leases. The transactions include the following: MNRK Music Group L.P., an independent music company, has agreed to a 7,629-square-foot lease at 443 Park Ave. South. The lease includes a seven-year, seven-month termt. Luke Dillmeier, Patrick Heeg, and Thomas Hines with Transwestern represented the tenant. AL Diamond Home Products LLC, an importer and distributor of household goods, has agreed to a 7,272-square-foot lease at 20 W. 36th St. The lease includes a seven-year, seven-month term. Joel Kubie with Benchmark represented the tenant. Kevin V. Lehman DDS, a New York City dental practice, has agreed to a 3,096-square-foot lease at 154 W. 14th St. The lease includes a 12-year, 10-month term. Todd Hershmann and Josh Gosin with Newmark represented the tenant. The post Koeppel Rosen Arranges Three Office Leases in Midtown, Midtown South appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Koeppel Rosen arranged ~18K SF across three office leases in Midtown/Midtown South.
Portfolio-level activity suggests stable tenant demand and recurring leasing velocity in central Manhattan.
Limited transaction detail; insufficient to assess market-level demand or rent trajectory.
stories.summary: Koeppel Rosen LLC, leasing agent for the Rosen family office portfolio, closed three separate office leases totaling nearly 18,000 SF across Midtown and Midtown South Manhattan properties. Max Koeppel represented the landlord on all transactions. No rent, tenant names, or lease terms disclosed.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily signal. Portfolio-level leasing activity in core Midtown suggests steady office demand, but lack of specificity (rents, submarkets, tenant profiles) limits ability to infer broader Manhattan market health or spillover effects on residential demand.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap Brokers Sale of 490-Unit Multifamily in St. Louis
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap announced the sale of Trinity Park Apartments, a 490-unit multifamily property in North St. Louis. The property was sold through an online live bid auction sale conducted by Marcus & Millichap. “Trinity Park Apartments offered investors a significant value-add opportunity,” said Ryan D. Engle, senior managing director investments. “The property’s below-market occupancy presented a substantial lease-up opportunity for the new ownership.” Engle, Andrean Angelov and Aaron Kuroiwa, investment specialists in Marcus & Millichap’s Chicago Oak Brook and Indianapolis offices, had the exclusive listing to market the property on behalf of the seller. Engle and Angelov, along with Mike Cusick in the firm’s St. Louis office, procured the buyer. The agents collaborated with Adam Sklaver and Philip Kates of Marcus & Millichap’s auction services to market the asset and assist in securing the buyer. Trinity Park Apartments, located at 11065 Dunklin Drive, spans 24.08 acres and consists of 34 residential buildings including 285 one-bedroom and 205 two-bedroom residences. If you’re reading about the multifamily industry, you should be in the room with its leaders. Connect Apartments brings together the executives featured in Connect CRE’s coverage for an afternoon of high-level insights and unmatched networking on September 22 at The Biltmore in LA. The post Marcus & Millichap Brokers Sale of 490-Unit Multifamily in St. Louis appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Trinity Park Apartments, 490 units in North St. Louis, sold via auction with below-market occupancy.
Asset marketed as value-add opportunity with significant lease-up potential for new owner.
St. Louis multifamily continues to attract acquisition interest despite occupancy challenges.
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap brokered the auction sale of Trinity Park Apartments (490 units, 34 buildings, 24.08 acres at 11065 Dunklin Drive, North St. Louis). The property was underoccupied at sale, presenting a lease-up value-add for the new owner. The deal closed via online live-bid auction conducted by Marcus & Millichap's Chicago, Indianapolis, and St. Louis offices.
stories.impact: Below-market occupancy and distressed auction pricing in North St. Louis signal softer demand or previous operator underperformance in the submarket. New ownership's lease-up play suggests confidence in achievable stabilized rents and demographic fundamentals, but caution warranted on St. Louis's regional job/population trends. Worth monitoring whether lease-up succeeds and at what rent levels—can inform forward development feasibility in the St. Louis market.

stories.title: Hanover Company Launches Construction on Its First SoCal Industrial
stories.excerpt: Hanover Company, alongside its capital partner, a real estate fund advised by Crow Holdings Capital, has begun construction on a ground-up industrial development in Simi Valley. The project marks the developer’s debut in the region. The approximately 200,000-square-foot building sits on a 13-acre site at 903 Quimisa Dr. With immediate proximity to CA 118, the project will feature 36’ clear heights, an 8.5” slab, skylights and ample employee parking. “We are thrilled to bring Hanover Industrial’s first project to Southern California and to establish a presence in the dynamic Simi Valley market,” said Anthony Feenick, development partner at Hanover Company. “We are grateful for our continued partnership with the team at Crow Holdings Capital on this endeavor and look forward to seeing the project come to fruition.” Located off the 118 freeway, the project is designed to accommodate a variety of users, including corporate headquarters, packaging and assembly or distribution. The post Hanover Company Launches Construction on Its First SoCal Industrial appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Hanover Company and Crow Holdings Capital breaking ground on 200K SF industrial in Simi Valley, CA.
First SoCal project for Hanover; speculative industrial development with 36' heights, flexible user accommodates logistics/assembly/HQ.
Capital partnership with Crow Holdings signals institutional backing and confidence in Southern California industrial fundamentals.
stories.summary: Hanover Company, partnered with Crow Holdings Capital, has started construction on a ground-up 200,000 SF industrial building on 13 acres in Simi Valley, CA (903 Quimisa Dr., near CA 118). The property features 36-foot clear heights, 8.5-inch slab, skylights, and parking; designed for distribution, assembly, packaging, or corporate HQ tenants. This marks Hanover's debut in Southern California.
stories.impact: Industrial growth in Simi Valley (Ventura County) suggests strong logistics/fulfillment demand in the Los Angeles region. Successful lease-up attracts downstream job creation and worker migration into the area, which would support multifamily demand in Ventura County and surrounding submarkets. Monitor tenant profile and absorption timeline; if major e-commerce or last-mile operator leases this space, signals potential residential upside in proximity and feeder markets (e.g., Moorpark, Ojai corridors).

stories.title: Associated Bank Finalizes Loan for Twelve-Acre Retail Project in OH
stories.excerpt: Associated Bank announced the completion of a $9 million loan to GTZ Properties for development of Trailhead Crossing, a multi-building retail project at 1135-1131 US-36 in Delaware, Ohio, a suburb of Columbus. The twelve-acre project will consist of three freestanding buildings occupied by Chik-Fil-A, Chipotle Mexican Grill and Take 5 Oil Change; a second three-tenant strip will be occupied by Dunkin Donuts, Nothing Bundt Cakes and Pacific Dental Services. Of two pad-ready sites, one is already pending sale to a national daycare company. A later phase of the development will be anchored by a big-box national retailer. GTZ Properties is a Highland Park, Illinois, based full-service commercial real estate development and investment company specializing in retail-related properties nationwide that is headed by Mitch Goltz and Jeremy Forman. Daniel Barrins, a senior vice president with Associated Bank’s Commercial Real Estate division in Chicago, managed the loan arrangements and closing. This is Associated Bank’s 18th loan to GTZ Properties principal Mitch Goltz. The post Associated Bank Finalizes Loan for Twelve-Acre Retail Project in OH appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Associated Bank closed $9M loan for Trailhead Crossing retail project in Delaware, Ohio (Columbus suburb).
Multi-phase development: initial three buildings (Chick-fil-A, Chipotle, Take 5), second strip (Dunkin, Nothing Bundt Cakes, Pacific Dental), plus daycare and future big-box anchor.
Retail fundamentals in Columbus-area suburbs support national tenant anchors and mixed-use positioning.
stories.summary: Associated Bank finalized a $9 million construction loan to GTZ Properties for Trailhead Crossing, a 12-acre retail project at 1135–1131 US-36 in Delaware, Ohio (Columbus suburb). Phase 1 includes six tenants (Chick-fil-A, Chipotle, Take 5, Dunkin, Nothing Bundt Cakes, Pacific Dental Services); a pad-ready site is pending sale to a national daycare; Phase 2 will feature a big-box anchor. This is Associated Bank's 18th loan to GTZ Properties principal Mitch Goltz.
stories.impact: Retail and daycare expansion in Columbus suburbs signal job creation and residential demographic influx. Multifamily developers should monitor Delaware, Ohio and adjacent submarkets (Westerville, New Albany, Powell corridors) for emerging residential demand. Daycare facility especially signals young-family migration; pairs with retail gravity to support Class B/C multifamily infill or new development in the submarket.

stories.title: Planet Fitness to Open at Sky Three Residences in West Brighton Beach
stories.excerpt: Planet Fitness has signed a lease for 14,520 square feet of retail space at the base of Tower 3 at Sky Three Residences, 532 Neptune Ave. in Brooklyn’s West Brighton Beach neighborhood. Located along the Neptune Avenue corridor, the new gym will complement the neighborhood’s growing mix of retail uses and is expected to open in early 2027. CBRE represented Planet Fitness in the transaction, while Commercial Acquisitions represented the landlord. Planet Fitness will join Sky Three’s growing ground-floor retail lineup, which includes CVS Pharmacy, NetCost Market, Starbucks, Flower Heaven NYC, Sky Mocha and Kings Barbershop. Flower Heaven offers Sky Three residents an exclusive 10% discount, while Sky Mocha provides delivery throughout the property’s amenity spaces, including directly to its resort-style pool. The post Planet Fitness to Open at Sky Three Residences in West Brighton Beach appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Planet Fitness signed 14.5K SF lease at Sky Three Residences, West Brighton Beach, Brooklyn; opens early 2027.
Mixed-use residential tower anchoring ground-floor retail (gym, pharmacy, grocer, coffee, specialty) to capture resident and neighborhood traffic.
Retail amenitization at multifamily base signals strong unit economics and resident retention at Sky Three.
stories.summary: Planet Fitness leased 14,520 SF at the base of Tower 3 at Sky Three Residences (532 Neptune Ave., West Brighton Beach, Brooklyn). The gym opening early 2027 joins existing tenants CVS, NetCost Market, Starbucks, Flower Heaven, Sky Mocha, and Kings Barbershop. CBRE represented Planet Fitness; Commercial Acquisitions represented the landlord.
stories.impact: Multifamily-anchored retail at scale (fitness, grocery, pharmacy, dining) indicates strong resident demand and developer confidence in Brooklyn waterfront submarkets. Sky Three's retail mix (especially food/beverage bundled with branded fitness) demonstrates premium amenitization strategy to justify rents and support absorption. West Brighton Beach densification and retail maturity signal continued residential desirability; worth tracking for nearby multifamily infill or redevelopment opportunities as neighborhood gentrifies.

stories.title: Sheppard Takes 107K SF at In-Rel’s D.C. Redevelopment
stories.excerpt: One of the 50 highest-grossing law firms in the U.S. has signed an anchor lease at a planned Washington, D.C., trophy office redevelopment three years before its anticipated completion. Law firm Sheppard signed for 107,224 square feet at In-Rel Properties’ 2033 K Street NW, CBRE announced Tuesday. The firm, which has more than 1,200 attorneys across 16 offices, will move in after the building’s expected completion in July 2029. The brokerage did not disclose the value of the lease or the asking rent. In-Rel is expanding and updating the existing building, located along K Street near the intersection of D.C.’s Central Business District, West End and Dupont Circle. The developer will retain the property’s concrete structure while expanding it vertically and horizontally, including adding three floors and a penthouse. The renovations are another example of owners betting on Washington’s bifurcated office market, where distress coexists with a shortage of large, new trophy spaces, particularly for law firms and other high-end tenants. “We all know D.C. has plenty of office space, but what it doesn’t have is enough large-block, trophy-quality product that leading law firms like Sheppard demand,” In-Rel CEO Jackson Siegal said in a statement. Sheppard Chair Luca Salvi said the new office would provide a more modern and efficient workplace as the firm approaches its centennial and continues growing its Washington operation. CBRE’s Dimitri Hajimihalis, Emily Eppolito and Carroll Cavanagh represented In-Rel. Savills’ Gary Stein, David Lipson, Jon Glass and Owen Jaccard represented Sheppard. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Law firm Sheppard (50 top-50 U.S. firms, 1,200+ attorneys) pre-leases 107.2K SF at In-Rel's 2033 K Street NW, D.C.
Trophy office redevelopment: add 3 floors, penthouse; concrete structure retained; completion July 2029.
Major anchor tenant 3+ years pre-lease signals confidence in D.C. office recovery and Class A demand near Central Business District.
stories.summary: Sheppard, a top-50 law firm with 1,200+ attorneys across 16 offices, signed an anchor lease for 107,224 SF at In-Rel Properties' planned 2033 K Street NW redevelopment in Washington, D.C., scheduled to complete July 2029. In-Rel is expanding the existing structure with three additional floors, a penthouse, and comprehensive renovations while retaining the concrete core. No rent disclosed. The lease reflects in-Rel's bet on D.C.'s bifurcated office market where trophy space is scarce despite pockets of distress.
stories.impact: Major legal firm pre-leasing trophy office in D.C. CBD/West End signals institutional confidence in office market recovery and high-end tenant stickiness. D.C. job markets (government, law, finance, tech) remain resilient. Downstream multifamily opportunity: law-firm employment anchors upscale residential demand in walkable D.C. submarkets (Dupont Circle, Logan Circle, NoMa). Monitor In-Rel's delivery timeline and post-completion absorption to gauge broader office-to-residential spillover in D.C. corridor.

stories.title: Eliot Spitzer Gains State Approval to Redevelop 985 Fifth Avenue After Legal Bout
stories.excerpt: Former New York Gov. Eliot Spitzer will finally get to demolish 985 Fifth Avenue after suing the state to obtain approval. Spitzer claimed that the state’s Division of Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) was delaying the approval of an application to not renew rent-stabilized leases in the building, a necessary step before the property could be redeveloped. Spitzer ultimately won the state’s blessing. The two-year request to end the rent-stabilized leases on the property followed approval from the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission in 2023 to take a wrecking ball to the 25-story rental property and construct luxury condominiums in its place. Spitzer alleged potential misconduct in the lawsuit, reported by The Real Deal. Spitzer could not be reached for comment. HCR, now under the administration of Gov. Kathy Hochul, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Spitzer’s Spitzer Enterprises has been advancing on other aspects of the project despite the delay, unveiling designs by SLCE Architects for the property in November 2025 which would yield 25 condo units, according to New York YIMBY. The former governor, who resigned in 2008 during a prostitution scandal, has owned the property since at least 2018 after buying seven residential buildings in the city, including 800 Fifth Avenue, with a total of 1.5 million square feet. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Eliot Spitzer wins state approval to demolish 985 Fifth Avenue and redevelop into luxury condos.
Two-year battle to end rent-stabilized leases resolved; NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission approved wrecking in 2023.
Demonstrates regulatory path for Manhattan luxury residential redevelopment from class rental stock.
stories.summary: Former New York Gov. Eliot Spitzer obtained state approval from New York's Division of Homes and Community Renewal (HCR) to demolish the 25-story rent-stabilized rental building at 985 Fifth Avenue and redevelop it as luxury condominiums. The approval followed a two-year legal battle over lease-non-renewal and NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission approval (2023). Spitzer Enterprises has already commissioned designs by SLCE Architects and advanced other project phases.
stories.impact: Marginal impact on multifamily development (luxury condo conversion is outside core multifamily). However, this signals regulatory willingness to permit rent-stabilized-to-luxury conversions on the Upper East Side, which could signal shifting political/regulatory appetite for destabilization. Multifamily developers should note the precedent: successful legal challenge and long timeline (2+ years) required; NYC rent-regulation reform remains a hostile environment for new multifamily supply on prime Manhattan sites.

stories.title: OCVibe Adds Five Dining Concepts to $5B SoCal District
stories.excerpt: The Samueli family has added five more dining concepts to the 50,000-square-foot market hall set to open next year as part of the $5 billion mixed-use development called OCVibe surrounding the Honda Center in Anaheim, Calif. Don Churros Gomez, MFK | Modern Filipino Kitchen, Mojo, Pull & Roll and Gelato Paradiso are the five new food options, adding Mexican, Filipino, Northern Chinese and Italian menus to the 21-kitchen market hall named Katella Commons. They join a growing roster at OCVibe, which earlier added concepts from chefs behind Amiga Amore, Burritos La Palma, Evil Cooks, Manaao Thai Comfort Food and Darkroom Restaurant and Wine Bar. Beloved Los Angeles chef Roy Choi is also bringing his Best Friend restaurant to the district. OCVibe did not disclose the values of the leases or the sizes of each space. Sources familiar with the development told Commercial Observer that OCVibe is fronting the initial investment, which averages around $300,000 per stall, as well as providing ongoing operational supports. “We wanted to approach this differently than a traditional landlord-tenant relationship,” OCVibe Senior Vice President Scott Frick said in a statement shared with CO. “Independent chefs are often asked to take on significant financial and operational risk before they ever serve their first meal. And unfortunately, many restaurants fail because of the significant upfront investment required of them.” Indeed, Frick recently told Commercial Observer that the Samueli family’s ownership structure has allowed the project to take a hands-on approach to restaurant leasing. Ownership is funding Katella Commons down to the kitchen equipment, allowing tenants to avoid substantial upfront costs of fitting out the new spaces. “Any tenant that comes in doesn’t have to come in with capital to fit out the kitchen — basically bring in your own knives and we’ll turn on the menu boards,” Frick said. bullets: OCVibe (Samueli family, $5B mixed-use, Anaheim) adds five dining concepts to 50K SF market hall (Katella Commons).
Anchor: Honda Center; market hall opening 2025; OCVibe fronting ~$300K/stall capex plus operational support.
Large mixed-use district attracts national chef talent and experiential retail; signals strong demographic/spending power in Orange County.
stories.summary: The Samueli family's OCVibe, a $5 billion mixed-use district around the Honda Center in Anaheim, CA, is adding five dining concepts (Don Churros Gomez, MFK Modern Filipino Kitchen, Mojo, Pull & Roll, Gelato Paradiso) to its 50,000 SF market hall, Katella Commons, opening next year. OCVibe is funding ~$300K capex per stall and providing operational support. Chef Roy Choi's Best Friend restaurant and other acclaimed concepts are also joining the lineup.
stories.impact: Large mixed-use development in Anaheim signals strong Orange County growth trajectory and spending power. Experiential retail and dining (market hall model) attracts younger, affluent demographics and leisure traffic. Multifamily developers should monitor OCVibe's phasing and execution; successful activation near Honda Center could drive residential demand in central/northern Orange County (Anaheim, Santa Ana, Garden Grove submarkets) for both Class A (near retail/entertainment) and Class B workforce housing (service workers).

stories.title: The New School Sells Loeb Hall Residence to Hawkins Way Capital for $52M
stories.excerpt: In its third acquisition of student housing in Manhattan this summer, Hawkins Way Capital has purchased a residence hall near Union Square for $51.5 million from the New School, according to city records made public Tuesday. Hawkins, using the entity 135 E 12th Owner, bought Loeb Hall, a 268-bed residence hall at 131-135 East 12th Street, directly from The New School, records show. Joshua Bird, managing director and general counsel at Hawkins, signed the deal for the buyer, while Loretta Ferrari, chief financial officer at the New School, signed for the seller. “We’ve long been looking for the right opportunity in this neighborhood, and this property represents an ideal addition to our portfolio,” Ross Walker, managing partner at Hawkins, said in a statement to Commercial Observer. “Its location, existing student housing infrastructure and flexibility put us in an ideal position to deliver high-quality accommodations in one of the country’s strongest urban student housing markets.” It’s unclear why the New School stopped using Loeb Hall as an active dormitory for its students, but the property was removed from its undergraduate housing options this year. Loeb Hall is four blocks east of the New School’s main University Center and administrative offices on Fifth Avenue, although the sprawling urban campus has numerous sites near Union Square. The former Loeb Hall will undergo renovations and be repositioned under Hawkins’ Found Study student housing platform, according to a spokesperson for Hawkins. It’s unclear who brokered the recent sale. A spokesperson for the New School did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The deal is Hawkins’ third major student housing acquisition in Manhattan in recent months. bullets: Hawkins Way Capital acquired Loeb Hall, 268-bed student residence, from New School for $51.5M in Manhattan.
Third student housing acquisition by Hawkins in Manhattan this summer; location near Union Square.
Institutional investor capital flowing into Manhattan student housing; New School divesting residential assets.
stories.summary: Hawkins Way Capital purchased Loeb Hall (268 beds) at 131–135 East 12th Street (near Union Square) from The New School for $51.5 million, using entity 135 E 12th Owner. This is Hawkins' third Manhattan student housing acquisition in summer 2024. The deal indicates institutional appetite for student housing in high-demand urban markets despite broader market headwinds.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact; student housing is a distinct asset class. However, The New School's divestiture of residential real estate suggests universities are exiting real estate ownership and management—potential opportunity for third-party operators to acquire/manage other campus-proximate housing in NYC. Monitor if other NYC universities follow suit. Hawkins' aggressive acquisition pace signals strong student housing returns in Manhattan near major universities (NYU, Cooper Union, The New School cluster), which may crowd out or elevate land/acquisition costs in East Village/Gramercy submarkets for standard multifamily development.
